notes: SnapApps now has its own web address, snapapps.gaiada.com. The old address keeps working and takes you to the new one. Your account, receipts and settings are exactly as they were.

SnapApps is part of GOD (Global Omni Data), and Settings now has an About GOD section with a link to god.gaiada.com. Tap GOD apps there to jump to YourTal and Free Tax Returns, or to your Spambank inbox if you have one. Nothing about you is sent when you tap.
SnapApp is now called SnapApps, to match our logo. Nothing else changes: your account, receipts and settings are exactly as they were.

SnapApp has a new look. The app icon is now the orange Snap Apps shutter with a receipt inside, and the app is orange throughout, in light and dark mode. Orange text and buttons are tuned so they stay easy to read, and the colours for danger and warnings are now easy to tell apart from the brand orange.

Your own Spambank inbox is now in the app. Open Mail from the menu, switch it on to get your own address, then read, write, search and sort your email without leaving SnapApp. Marketing mail is filed into Spam and Junk, and Unsubscribe stops a sender in one tap.

Year in Analytics and Export receipts now follows your tax year. In an Australian workspace it runs from 1 July to today, labelled like 2026-27 financial year, so an export lines up with your tax return. Indonesian workspaces keep the calendar year.

A valid receipt in a personal or household workspace no longer says its GST credit is claimable. Personal workspaces cannot claim GST, so it now just says the receipt meets the ATO requirements for a tax invoice. Business workspaces still show the credit.

Your work receipts can now go to Free Tax Returns. Open a receipt and choose a work category on the new Tax return card, and it counts in your deductions for that financial year. Bought something for work with your other shopping? Tick just that line and pick its category. Sign in with YourTal now works in the web app too, and Mileage shows the rate per kilometre correctly.

Signing in is simpler: one Continue with YourTal button takes you in, whether you are new or already have an account. If you signed up with your email, choose Sign in with email instead. Snap Apps now lives at snapapp.gaiada.com, and coming back from YourTal opens the app again.

Rupiah amounts now read correctly: a receipt printed Rp 74.000 is saved as seventy-four thousand, not 74. If a month has no spending in your workspace’s currency, the home screen says so and tells you how many receipts are in another currency, instead of showing $0. If you leave to confirm your email while creating a YourTal account, coming back now finishes signing you in, and tax totals use your workspace’s own tax name.

This build is signed with Snap Apps’ own private key instead of the shared test key, so Android will not install it over your current app. Before updating, open the app and let any snaps still waiting send, then uninstall Snap Apps and install this version from the download page. You only need to do this once; later updates install over it as before.

Each snap is one page, and a scan needs a credit. When credits run out the app says so and offers to buy more; snaps already sent are kept and read once you have credits again. Buying credits now goes through a card checkout (simulated on this test build, so no real money moves). Settings can delete your account, and the trip recorder explains why it asks for your location before Android does.

You can now sign in or create an account with YourTal, and link YourTal so receipts scanned with bought credits earn points. Each scan uses one credit, free ones first, and a scan we cannot read gives its credit back. Amounts now show in your workspace’s own currency, so an Indonesian workspace reads in Rupiah (Rp). Credit prices stay in Australian dollars, because that is what Snap Apps charges.

You can now reset a forgotten password by email, and a new account confirms its email address. Sessions now expire, so after a long time away you may be asked to sign in again, and Settings can sign you out on every device at once. Help now shows your version and build, so a problem report says which one you have.

Snap Apps has a new look: a bar along the bottom of every screen with Scan raised in the middle, white cards and a new typeface. A photo you take with no signal is kept on your phone and sent when you are back online. Settings now shows your version and build, and the update card tells you what is new. Screens that are not finished yet, such as the wallet, alerts and rewards, are hidden for now.
